questions.q: What is an Ethereum account nonce?
options: A per-account, strictly sequential counter that increments by one with each transaction it sends
A random cryptographic value generated for every transaction
The amount of gas a transaction is allowed to consume
A unique ID assigned by the node provider, not the protocol
questions.explain: Despite the name, an Ethereum nonce isn't about randomness — it's a simple incrementing counter used purely to order and de-duplicate an account's transactions.

questions.q: Why does one stuck transaction (say, nonce 3) block every later transaction from the same account?
options: A node won't include a transaction at nonce N+1 until nonce N from that sender has already landed
Ethereum only allows one pending transaction per account at a time by protocol rule
Later transactions are automatically cancelled when an earlier one is slow
It doesn't — later nonces confirm independently of earlier ones
questions.explain: Nonces must be consumed in strict order, so nonce 4 and 5 can't be included until nonce 3 confirms, regardless of how valid they are on their own.

questions.q: When should a backend query the nonce with the "pending" block tag instead of "latest"?
options: When it's sending several transactions back-to-back, so it accounts for transactions still in the mempool and avoids a nonce collision
Only when connected to a testnet, never on mainnet
Never — "pending" always returns an invalid nonce
Only when reading contract state, not when sending transactions
questions.explain: "latest" only counts mined transactions; "pending" also counts the mempool, which matters when multiple sends could otherwise race onto the same nonce.

questions.q: What happens if you set a transaction's gas limit too low?
options: It reverts with an out-of-gas error partway through, and you still pay for the gas consumed before it failed
The transaction is automatically resized by the network to a valid gas limit
The transaction is queued and retried later for free
Nothing — gas limit only affects speed, not success
questions.explain: Running out of gas mid-execution causes a revert, but the gas already spent up to that point is still consumed and paid for.

questions.q: How do you "speed up" or "cancel" a stuck transaction?
options: Send a new transaction with the exact same nonce and a higher gas price
Delete the transaction from the mempool using a special RPC method
Wait for it to expire automatically after 24 hours
Lower the gas price on the original transaction
questions.explain: The network treats the newer, same-nonce transaction as the real one for that slot; "cancel" is the same trick, just sending 0 ETH to yourself instead of the original call.
